newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: North Korean defector defends his sanity.
newsitem.headline: North Korean defector defends his sanity.

text.p: South Korea on Thursday released a handwritten note it said was written by a North Korean defector that lashes out at Pyongyang for causing starvation and seeking confrontation with the South.

"Starting with my family, people will judge that I'm mad," said the letter signed by Hwang Jang-yop, now inside South Korea's consulate compound in Beijing. "But the question is: am I the only mad person?"
"I tormented and tormented over this," Hwang wrote. He added that to "save our people from misfortune" he decided to leave and hold talks with Southern officials.

Hwang attacked those in the North who continued to treat South Korea as the enemy and talked of turning it into a "sea of fire" while proposing national unification. "How could you regard this as the behaviour of sane people?"
"Also, how could you call people sane who loudly talk about building an ideal society for workers and farmers while workers and farmers are starving?"
But Hwang said North Korea was in no danger of collapse, and at one point defended the ruling Worker's Party from which he received "love and consideration".
